title: Our Story
description: How Osman Mohammed and his family turned their experience in software, teaching, and business into practical AI education.
html:
Osman Academy/Our Story
Our Story

AI changed my work. Learning brought us here.

I had spent more than seven years building software when AI began doing parts of the work I was paid to do. Becoming a beginner again led my family and me to build Osman Academy.

The turning point

When my work began to change

I remember eagerly waiting to try ChatGPT. When I finally did, my first reaction was: Subhan Allah. I knew language models could make mistakes, but using one still felt unlike any software I had known.

As coding assistants improved, I began using them every day. They were becoming capable at writing code. Writing, testing, and deploying that code was my bread and butter.

I could see my own work changing, and I needed to change with it.

I'm Osman Mohammed, an AI Solution Architect. My path began with Electrical and Electronics Engineering in India. After graduating, I worked as a contractor on Google Maps, finding house numbers in Street View images and typing what I could see. It was data labeling, although I didn't think of it that way then. I still don't know whether those images trained a particular system.

A master's degree in Computer Science and Information Technology in the United States led me into software engineering. Years later, AI brought me back to a question I hadn't expected to face: how do I begin again?

The hard part

Learning to be a beginner again

Years of writing and maintaining software had given me a mental map of the systems I worked on. I understood them because I had lived with the code. Working with AI meant rethinking familiar habits.

I had to learn how to explain what I wanted, understand what a system produced, test it, and decide whether the result was sound. My experience still mattered, but I had new skills to practice.

Even choosing where to learn was difficult. There was so much material, and I wasn't sure which sources to trust. I focused on resources from Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI, then practiced with real tools to understand the ideas that carried across their products.

Building it together

My learning became a family project

I took notes as I learned, but they were organized mainly for me. My wife, Firdous Osman, saw how much clearer the journey could be. With her experience in teaching and instructional design, she helped me think about how to introduce an idea, where a learner might get stuck, and what practice would help it make sense.

My brother, Abdul Bari Mohammed, brought questions from business analysis: which parts of a workflow could AI help with? What would need to change? How would we judge whether it worked?

I understood software systems. Firdous understood how people learn. Bari understood business processes. Together, we began turning what we learned into e-books, hands-on projects, and courses for people facing similar questions.

This is personal, too. Firdous is my partner in this work and in raising our family. Osman Academy is in her name. We want to build something useful for others and earn a living from that work. Both hopes are part of why we began.

What we learned

Understanding comes before confidence

Working with AI taught me to keep asking questions: have I understood the problem? Does this result make sense? How can I test it? People still need to guide the work and take responsibility for what they build.

That experience shapes our teaching. We begin with the foundations, make room for practice, and ask learners to explain their thinking. The aim is to help people build useful AI systems with understanding and sound judgment.

Our purpose

Learning that starts with people.

Our mission

Teach the knowledge and wisdom to build AI systems that align with human interests.

Our vision

A more peaceful and prosperous world, where people use AI with understanding and sound judgment.

Our objectives

Explain concepts clearly, connect learning to practical work, and help learners explain what they understand in their own words.

How we teach

How learning becomes practice

Could you explain what you just learned to a family member or friend? That is our starting point for checking understanding.

Our four steps connect knowledge with judgment: learn a concept, practice it, apply it to a realistic decision, and bring it together in a project.

01
Knowledge

Learn

Watch the lesson, then clarify the concept with reading and visual guides until the idea is solid.

02
Knowledge

Practice

Check what you recall, then rehearse the skill in a guided, low-risk setting with real feedback.

03
Wisdom

Apply

Put judgment to the test in role-play scenarios and realistic assignments — the kind of decisions you'd actually face outside the course.

04
Wisdom

Master

Prove it through a capstone project that puts everything you've learned, knowledge and wisdom both, to work.

Your next step

So, will AI take your job?

Honestly, I don't know. I do know that seeing my own work change pushed me to learn. I wanted to understand what these systems could do and where my judgment still mattered.

If you're asking similar questions, start with AI Fundamentals. We'll begin with the foundations that helped me make sense of the changes in my own work, one concept at a time.
